questions.question: In June 2025, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted to reduce the policy repo rate by 50 basis points (bps) with immediate effect to:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.50%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**, in its meeting held in **June 2025**, decided to reduce the **policy repo rate** to **5.50%**.
 
• This decision involved a significant reduction of **50 basis points (bps)** from the existing rate, aimed at fostering an environment conducive to economic expansion.
 
• By lowering the **repo rate** to **5.50%**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** intends to decrease the cost of borrowing for commercial banks, which typically translates into lower lending rates for businesses and individual consumers.
 
• The **MPC** usually meets **bi-monthly** (every **two months**) to evaluate the macroeconomic situation, including **inflation** levels and **GDP growth** projections, to determine the appropriate policy stance.
 
• The reduction to **5.50%** indicates an **accommodative monetary policy stance**, which is often used during periods when the central bank wants to encourage spending and investment to boost the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**:

 
 
• The **MPC** is a statutory and institutionalized framework under the **Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934**, specifically Section **45ZB**, to maintain **price stability**.
 
• It consists of **six members**: **three members** from the **RBI** (including the **Governor**) and **three external members** appointed by the **Central Government**.
 
• The **Governor of the RBI** acts as the **ex-officio Chairperson** of the committee.
 
 
 
• **Policy Repo Rate**:
 
 
• The **Repo Rate** (Repurchase Rate) is the interest rate at which the **RBI** lends liquidity to commercial banks against the collateral of government and other approved securities.
 
• It is the primary tool used by the central bank to control the **money supply** and **liquidity** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Basis Points (bps)**:
 
 
• In finance, a **basis point** is a common unit of measure for interest rates. **One basis point** is equivalent to **0.01%** or **1/100th of a percent**.
 
• Therefore, a reduction of **50 bps** is equal to a **0.50%** decrease in the interest rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Inflation Targeting**: The **RBI** has a primary mandate to keep **Consumer Price Index (CPI)** inflation within a target of **4%** with a tolerance band of **+/- 2%** (i.e., between **2%** and **6%**).
 
• **Liquidity Management**: Besides the **Repo Rate**, the **RBI** uses other instruments like the **Reverse Repo Rate**, **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**, and **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** to manage the economy.
 
• **Impact of Rate Cuts**: A lower repo rate of **5.50%** generally makes **EMIs** (Equated Monthly Installments) for **home loans**, **car loans**, and **personal loans** more affordable, thereby increasing the disposable income of households.
 
• **Decision Making**: In the **MPC**, each member has **one vote**. In the event of a tie, the **Governor** has a **casting vote**.

questions.question: Which of the following was launched by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy in September 2025, aligning with India’s Net Zero and renewable energy goals?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**National Policy on Geothermal Energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Policy on Geothermal Energy** was officially launched by the **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** in **September 2025**. This policy marks a significant milestone in India's transition toward a diversified and sustainable energy portfolio. ***Hence, the correct answer is National Policy on Geothermal Energy.***
 
• The primary objective of this policy is to harness **geothermal energy**, which is the heat stored beneath the Earth's surface, to provide a consistent and **baseload power supply** that complements intermittent sources like solar and wind.
 
• The policy aligns with India’s ambitious **Net Zero** target by the **year 2070** and the intermediate goal of achieving **500 GW** of **non-fossil fuel** based energy capacity by **2030**.
 
• It introduces a structured framework for the **exploration, assessment, and commercial exploitation** of geothermal resources across various geothermal provinces in India.
 
• The framework encourages **Public-Private Partnerships (PPP)** and offers financial incentives and **Single Window Clearance** to attract domestic and international investments in deep-drilling technologies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Geothermal Energy Potential in India:**
 
 
• India is estimated to have a **geothermal potential** of approximately **10,000 MW (10 GW)**.
 
• Major geothermal provinces include the **Himalayas (Puga, Chhumathang)**, **Sohna valley**, **Cambay basin**, **Son-Narmada-Tapti (SONATA) lineament belt**, and the **Godavari and Mahanadi basins**.
 
• The **Puga Valley** in **Ladakh** is considered the most promising site, where the first pilot project was initiated by **ONGC (Oil and Natural Gas Corporation)**.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE):**
 
 
• The **MNRE** is the nodal ministry of the **Government of India** for all matters relating to new and renewable energy.
 
• It aims to develop and deploy new and renewable energy for supplementing the energy requirements of the country.
 
• The ministry plays a pivotal role in implementing the **National Green Hydrogen Mission** and the **PM-KUSUM** scheme.
 
 
 
• **India's Climate Commitments:**
 
 
• At **COP26** in **Glasgow**, India announced the **Panchamrit** strategy, which includes increasing non-fossil energy capacity and reducing the **carbon intensity** of the economy by **45%** by **2030**.
 
• Geothermal energy is vital as it provides **24/7 clean energy**, unlike **Solar Energy** (dependent on daylight) or **Wind Energy** (dependent on weather conditions).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Advantages of Geothermal Power:**
 
 
• It has a **high capacity factor**, often exceeding **80%**, making it a reliable **baseload** alternative to coal-fired plants.
 
• It requires **minimal land area** compared to large-scale solar farms or wind parks.
 
• Applications include not just electricity generation but also **direct heat use** for space heating, greenhouses, and industrial processes.
 
 
 
• **Technological Requirements:**
 
 
• The policy emphasizes the use of **Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS)** and **Binary Cycle Power Plants** to extract energy from low-to-medium temperature reservoirs found in many parts of India.

questions.question: In June 2025, the Government of India planned to shut down the National Polio Surveillance Network (NPSN) established by which international organisation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Health Organization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Polio Surveillance Network (NPSN)** was established in **1997** as a collaborative effort between the **Government of India** and the **World Health Organization (WHO)** to provide technical assistance for polio eradication.
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Government of India** plans to complete the transition of the **NPSN**, effectively shutting down the **WHO**-managed framework to integrate its functions into the national public health system.
 
• The **NPSN** played a pivotal role in the **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI)**, utilizing a vast network of **Surveillance Medical Officers (SMOs)** to monitor **Acute Flaccid Paralysis (AFP)** cases across the country.
 
• Through the rigorous monitoring and immunization strategies supported by the **WHO**, **India** reported its last case of wild poliovirus in **January 2011** and was officially certified **Polio-free** in **March 2014**.
 
• The transition signifies **India's** capacity to independently manage large-scale **Vaccine Preventable Diseases (VPDs)** surveillance using its own institutional resources and manpower. ***Hence, the correct answer is World Health Organization.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **World Health Organization (WHO):**

 
 
• Established on **7 April 1948**, the **WHO** is a specialized agency of the **United Nations** responsible for international public health.
 
• Headquartered in **Geneva**, **Switzerland**, it works with **194 Member States** to promote health, keep the world safe, and serve the vulnerable.
 
• It provides technical support and sets international health standards, such as those used in the **NPSN** for polio surveillance.
 
 
 
• **Polio Eradication in India:**
 
 
• The last case of wild poliovirus was detected on **13 January 2011**, in a two-year-old girl in **Howrah**, **West Bengal**.
 
• **India** maintained a zero-case record for **three consecutive years**, meeting the **WHO** criteria for eradication.
 
• The **Pulse Polio Programme**, launched in **1995**, was the primary vehicle for administering the **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV)** to children under the **age** of **5**.
 
 
 
• **Transition and Repurposing:**
 
 
• The infrastructure developed by the **WHO** for polio is now being repurposed to strengthen surveillance for other diseases like **Measles**, **Rubella**, and **Neonatal Tetanus**.
 
• This shift is part of the **National Health Mission (NHM)** strategy to achieve universal immunization coverage across all **states** and **Union Territories**.
 
 
 
• **Global Polio Eradication Initiative (GPEI):**
 
 
• It is a public-private partnership led by national governments and five partners: **WHO**, **Rotary International**, the **US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)**, **UNICEF**, and the **Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Surveillance Mechanism:** The **NPSN** utilized nearly **40,000 reporting units** and over **1,000** specialized staff members to ensure no case of paralysis went unnoticed.
 
• **Polio Vaccines:** India utilizes both **Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV)** for mass campaigns and **Inactivated Polio Vaccine (IPV)** as part of the **Universal Immunization Programme (UIP)**.
 
• **Current Status:** While **India** is polio-free, the risk of importation remains from countries where the virus is still endemic, such as **Pakistan** and **Afghanistan**, necessitating continued vigilance.

questions.question: Which summit saw the participation of 16 states, the EU, and NATO in early March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**London Summit on Ukraine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **London Summit on Ukraine** was a high-level diplomatic event held in **early March 2025** in **London**, **United Kingdom**.
 
• This summit saw the active participation of **16 sovereign states**, including major global powers and regional allies committed to the stability of Eastern Europe.
 
• Crucially, the summit included the **European Union (EU)** and the **North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO)**, represented by their respective leadership, highlighting a unified multilateral approach.
 
• The primary objective of the summit was to coordinate **long-term security commitments** and provide a structured framework for **Ukraine's** defensive capabilities and future reconstruction. ***Hence, the statement regarding the participation of 16 states, the EU, and NATO is correct.***
 
• The meeting served as a follow-up to previous international conferences, focusing on the **economic recovery** and **infrastructure rebuilding** of the nation amidst ongoing geopolitical tensions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Strategic Importance of London:** The **United Kingdom** has consistently acted as a lead coordinator for international aid. By hosting the summit in **March 2025**, the **UK government** aimed to solidify bilateral security pacts that go beyond immediate military hardware assistance.
 
• **Role of NATO and EU:** 
 
 
• **NATO's** involvement centered on the **Interoperability** of defense systems and the transition of **Ukraine** toward **Alliance standards**.
 
• The **EU** focused on the **Ukraine Facility**, a multi-year financial package designed to support **governance reforms** and **economic integration** into the **Single Market**.
 
 
 
• **Defense Industry Collaboration:** A significant portion of the **2025 summit** was dedicated to **joint ventures** between **16 states** and **Ukrainian defense firms** to boost **ammunition production** and **drone technology**.
 
• **Participant Demographics:** The **16 states** involved primarily consisted of **G7 members** and key **Eastern European** and **Nordic-Baltic** nations, emphasizing a coalition of "willing and capable" partners.
 
• **Comparison with other Summits:** 
 
 
• The **Munich Security Conference** (typically held in **February**) serves as an informal platform for global security policy but lacks the specific legislative or financial mandate of the **London Summit**.
 
• The **Shangri-La Dialogue** is primarily focused on **Asia-Pacific** security and takes place in **Singapore**, usually in **May or June**.
 
• The **UN General Assembly** meets in **September** in **New York** and covers a much broader range of global humanitarian and developmental issues.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **London Summit on Ukraine** is part of a series of **Recovery Conferences**; previous iterations were held in **Lugano (2022)**, **London (2023)**, and **Berlin (2024)**.
 
• By **2025**, the focus shifted significantly from "emergency survival aid" to "sustainable investment" and **private sector engagement**.
 
• The participation of **NATO** and the **EU** at this specific summit in **March 2025** underscored the institutionalization of support, ensuring that aid remains independent of individual national election cycles.
 
• Specific outcomes included the **London Declaration 2025**, which outlined a **10-year roadmap** for **energy security** and **de-mining** operations across **Ukraine**.
</ul

questions.question: Which jurist was designated as the 53rd Chief Justice of India on 30 October 2025 and assumed office on 24 November 2025?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Justice Surya Kant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Justice Surya Kant** was officially designated as the **53rd Chief Justice of India (CJI)** on **30 October 2025** and formally assumed office on **24 November 2025**.
 
• He succeeded **Justice B.R. Gavai** (the **52nd CJI**), continuing the established line of succession in the **Supreme Court of India** based on the principle of seniority.
 
• Born in **Hisar, Haryana**, in **1962**, **Justice Surya Kant** has had a distinguished legal career, previously serving as the **Chief Justice of the Himachal Pradesh High Court** before his elevation to the **Supreme Court** on **24 May 2019**.
 
• His tenure as the **Chief Justice of India** is slated to last until **9 February 2027**, when he will reach the mandatory retirement age of **65 years**.
 
• During his career, he has been part of several landmark judgments involving **constitutional law**, **fundamental rights**, and **administrative reforms**, contributing significantly to Indian jurisprudence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Justice B.V. Nagarathna:** A sitting judge of the **Supreme Court of India**, she is widely recognized for the historic possibility of becoming the **first woman Chief Justice of India**. Her projected tenure as CJI is expected to begin in **September 2027**, though it will be for a relatively short duration of **36 days**.
 
• **Justice P.S. Narasimha:** He was elevated directly from the **Bar** to the **Supreme Court bench** in **August 2021**. He is also in the line of succession to become the **Chief Justice of India** in the **year 2027-28**.
 
• **Justice Vikram Nath:** Formerly the **Chief Justice of the Gujarat High Court**, he was among the nine judges appointed to the **Supreme Court** in **2021** and is another key figure in the seniority-based succession for the top judicial post.
 
• **Appointment Process:** Under **Article 124** of the **Constitution of India**, the **President of India** appoints the **Chief Justice**. By convention, the outgoing **CJI** recommends the name of the most senior judge of the **Supreme Court** as their successor.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Collegium System:** This is the system by which judges are appointed and transferred in the **Supreme Court** and **High Courts**. It consists of the **Chief Justice of India** and the four most senior judges of the **Supreme Court**.
 
• **Retirement and Qualifications:** A judge of the **Supreme Court** must be a citizen of **India** and must have been a judge of a **High Court** for at least **5 years** or an advocate of a **High Court** for **10 years**. The retirement age is fixed at **65 years**.
 
• **Constitutional Oath:** Every person appointed to be a judge of the **Supreme Court** shall, before entering upon office, make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before the **President of India** according to the form set out in the **Third Schedule** of the **Constitution**.
 
• **Removal:** A judge can only be removed from office by an order of the **President** passed after an address by each **House of Parliament** (supported by a special majority) on the grounds of **proved misbehaviour or incapacity**.
</ul

questions.question: Which Indian state was involved in a boundary dispute with Assam in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The boundary dispute between **Assam** and **Meghalaya** is a long-standing issue that traces back to **1972**, when **Meghalaya** was carved out of **Assam** under the **North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971**.
 
• The two states share a border of approximately **884.9 km**. The conflict primarily stems from **Meghalaya**'s challenge to the **Assam Reorganisation (Meghalaya) Act, 1969**, which defined the boundaries of the new state.
 
• There are **12 areas of dispute** along the border, including **Upper Tarabari**, **Gazang reserve forest**, **Hahim**, **Langpih**, **Borduar**, **Boklapara**, **Nongwah**, **Matamur**, **Khanapara-Pilangkata**, **Deshdemoreah**, **Block I and Block II**, and **Khanduli-Psyar**.
 
• In **March 2022**, a historic **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** was signed between **Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma** and **Meghalaya Chief Minister Conrad Sangma** in the presence of **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** to resolve **6** out of the **12** points of dispute.
 
• The dispute reached significant legal and administrative milestones in **2024** and **2025** as both state governments intensified the **second phase** of border talks to address the remaining **six complex sectors**, involving **regional committees** and **joint field visits**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Meghalaya.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Constitutional Provisions:** Under **Article 3** of the **Constitution of India**, the **Parliament** has the power to form new states and alter the areas, boundaries, or names of existing states. This power is often exercised to address administrative needs or settle historical territorial claims.
 
• **The North-Eastern Areas (Reorganisation) Act, 1971:** This was a landmark **Act** of the **Indian Parliament** that led to the creation of the states of **Manipur** and **Tripura**, and the conversion of the **Union Territories** of **Mizoram** and **Arunachal Pradesh**. It also formally established **Meghalaya** as a full-fledged state, having previously been an autonomous state within **Assam**.
 
• **Other Border Disputes in Northeast India:**
 
 
• **Assam-Mizoram:** A major dispute involving the **Inner Line Reserve Forest**, which saw a violent clash in **July 2021** resulting in the death of **six Assam Police personnel**.
 
• **Assam-Arunachal Pradesh:** A dispute involving over **1,200 villages**. A significant **Namsai Declaration** was signed in **2022** to minimize the number of contested areas.
 
• **Assam-Nagaland:** The longest-running border dispute in the region, which began immediately after **Nagaland** achieved statehood in **1963**, involving tracts in the **Brahmaputra Valley**.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA):** The **MHA** acts as a facilitator in inter-state boundary disputes. While the **Supreme Court** has jurisdiction under **Article 131** of the **Constitution** to decide on such disputes, the **Union Government** prefers settlements through **mutual dialogue** and **regional committees**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Survey of India:** This is the **national survey and mapping organization** of the country under the **Department of Science & Technology**. It plays a critical role in **demarcating boundaries** and providing **geospatial data** to resolve state-level territorial conflicts.
 
• **Criteria for Settlement:** The recent **Assam-Meghalaya** resolution process used **five principles**: **historical facts**, **ethnicity**, **administrative convenience**, **contiguity**, and the **willingness** of the local population residing in the disputed areas.
 
• **Status of Other Options:**
 
 
• **Himachal Pradesh:** While it has minor territorial discussions with **Ladakh** (Sarchu) and **Haryana** (Parwanoo), it was not a primary party in the **2025** high-profile **Assam** border context.
 
• **Sikkim:** Shares international borders with **China**, **Nepal**, and **Bhutan**, but does not share a land border with **Assam**.
 
• **Bihar:** Primarily involved in flood management or occasional transit issues with **Nepal** or **Uttar Pradesh**, but not a border disputant with **Assam**.
 
 
</ul

__
 
• The **NAVYA** programme is a strategic initiative launched by the **Government of India** to empower **adolescent girls** by providing them with specialized **vocational training**.

questions.question: In 2025, which two Indian cities were recognised as 'Wetland Cities'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Udaipur and Indore**__.

__
 
• The **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEF&CC)** officially submitted nominations for **Indore (Madhya Pradesh)**, **Udaipur (Rajasthan)**, and **Bhopal (Madhya Pradesh)** for the **Wetland City Accreditation (WCA)** under the **Ramsar Convention**.
 
• **Udaipur**, popularly known as the **City of Lakes**, is famous for its sophisticated lake system, including **Lake Pichola**, **Fateh Sagar**, and **Swaroop Sagar**, which are vital for the city's microclimate and tourism. ***Hence, the inclusion of Udaipur is correct.***
 
• **Indore** has been recognized for its environmental initiatives, particularly the restoration and protection of **Sirpur Wetland** and **Yashwant Sagar**, both of which are **Ramsar Sites**. ***Hence, the inclusion of Indore is correct.***
 
• The **Wetland City Accreditation** scheme was established to recognize cities that have taken exceptional steps to safeguard their urban wetlands and promote sustainable use.
 
• These nominations represent India's first-ever attempt to get its cities recognized on the global stage as **Wetland Cities**, highlighting the country's commitment to the **Amrit Dharohar** initiative. ***Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wetland City Accreditation (WCA):**
 
 
• This voluntary accreditation system was introduced during the **COP12** of the **Ramsar Convention** in **2015**.
 
• It aims to promote the conservation and wise use of **urban and peri-urban wetlands**, as well as sustainable socio-economic benefits for local populations.
 
• To be eligible, a city must have one or more **Ramsar Sites** or significant wetlands within its jurisdiction that provide various **ecosystem services**.
 
 
 
• **The Ramsar Convention:**
 
 
• Signed in **1971** in the Iranian city of **Ramsar**, it is one of the oldest inter-governmental accords for preserving the ecological character of wetlands.
 
• India currently has **85 Ramsar Sites** (as of 2024 updates), covering a significant area of the country's total geographical surface.
 
 
 
• **Specific City Highlights:**
 
 
• **Udaipur:** The lakes here are managed by the **Rajasthan Government** and local communities, ensuring a balance between urban development and ecological preservation.
 
• **Indore:** Known as India’s cleanest city, it has integrated waste management with wetland conservation, significantly improving the biodiversity of **Sirpur Lake**.
 
• **Bhopal:** Although not paired in the chosen option, it was also nominated due to the **Bhoj Wetland**, which consists of the **Upper Lake** and **Lower Lake**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Accreditation:** Gaining **Wetland City** status provides international prestige and helps cities attract funding for conservation projects and sustainable **eco-tourism**.
 
• **Conservation Laws:** In India, wetlands are protected under the **Wetlands (Conservation and Management) Rules, 2017**, which prohibit activities like encroachment, dumping of solid waste, and discharge of untreated effluents.
 
• **Global Context:** There are currently very few accredited **Wetland Cities** globally (mostly in China, France, and South Korea), and India's inclusion would mark a significant milestone for **South Asia**.
 
• **Year of Recognition:** While the nomination process gained momentum in **2024**, the official recognition status for the cycle is often finalized by the **Ramsar Secretariat** in the following year, matching the **2025** timeframe mentioned in the query.

• The **Union Budget 2025–26**, presented by Finance Minister **Nirmala Sitharaman** on **February 1, 2025**, has allocated a total of **₹13,416 crore** to the **Department of Space (DoS)**.

• The bulk of this budget is directed toward **Space Technology**, which received **₹10,131.63 crore**, primarily to fund ambitious missions like **Gaganyaan** and **Chandrayaan-4**.
 
• The **Gaganyaan** mission, India's first human spaceflight program, is a major priority, with funds earmarked for unmanned test flights and the development of heavy-lift launch vehicles.
 
• Other major allocations within the budget include **₹1,532.70 crore** for **Space Applications** and **₹588.63 crore** for the **INSAT** satellite system, which supports communication and weather monitoring.

• The **Department of Space** is the nodal agency for India's space program and reports directly to the **Prime Minister** of India.
 
• It oversees the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO)**, which is headquartered in **Bengaluru** and was established in **1969**.
 
• The **DoS** also manages **NewSpace India Limited (NSIL)** and the **Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Centre (IN-SPACe)** to foster commercial and private participation.
 
 
 
• **Long-term Vision (Amrit Kaal):**
 
 
• India aims to establish the **Bharatiya Antariksh Station** (Indian Space Station) by the year **2035**.
 
• The government has set a target to land the first **Indian astronaut** on the **Moon** by **2040**.
 
• The **Indian Space Policy 2023** serves as the guiding document for these milestones, encouraging **end-to-end** participation of the private sector in space activities.
 
 
 
• **Space Sector Reforms:**
 
 
• In **2024**, the government amended the **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** policy, allowing **100% FDI** in certain sub-sectors of the space industry to attract global investment.
 
• A **₹1,000 crore Venture Capital Fund** was also announced to support **space-tech startups**, aiming to expand India's share in the global space economy from **2%** to **10%** by **2033**.

• **Mission-Specific Highlights:**
 
 
• **Chandrayaan-4:** A sample-return mission to the **Moon** that will demonstrate docking and undocking capabilities in lunar orbit.
 
• **Shukrayaan:** A planned mission to explore the planet **Venus**, focusing on its atmosphere and surface chemistry.
 
• **NGLV (Next Generation Launch Vehicle):** Development of a reusable, heavy-lift rocket capable of carrying larger payloads for future space station modules.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The increased funding is expected to boost **high-tech manufacturing** and generate employment in the **STEM** (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics) sectors.
 
• India’s **Space Economy** is currently valued at approximately **$8.4 billion** and is projected to reach **$44 billion** within the next decade.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Union Budget 2025-26** continues to prioritize the **Khelo India - National Programme for Development of Sports**, which aims to identify talented players at the **grassroots level** and provide them with a platform to excel.
 
• A significant portion of the sports budget is allocated to the **Sports Authority of India (SAI)**, which is responsible for managing **National Centres of Excellence (NCOE)** and providing **high-performance coaching** to **young athletes** across the **country**.
 
• The government focuses on the development of **sports infrastructure**, including the construction of **synthetic tracks**, **multi-purpose indoor halls**, and **swimming pools** in both **urban and rural areas** to bridge the accessibility gap. ***Hence, the statement regarding nurturing young talent and infrastructure is correct.***
 
• The budget includes dedicated funds for the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, which provides **customized training**, **international exposure**, and **medical support** to **elite athletes** preparing for the **2028 Los Angeles Olympics**.
 
• The core philosophy of the **2025-26** allocation is to transform **India** into a multi-sport nation and support the **long-term vision** of hosting the **2036 Olympic Games**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Khelo India Scheme**:
 
 
• Launched in **2018** by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**, this scheme aims to revive the **sports culture** in **India** by integrating **sports with education**.
 
• It covers various components such as **Play Field Development**, **Community Coaching Development**, and **State Level Khelo India Centres**.
 
 
 
• **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**:
 
 
• Established in **September 2014**, it is a flagship program to provide **financial assistance** and **world-class facilities** to **potential medal winners**.
 
• The scheme is managed by the **Mission Olympic Cell (MOC)**, which evaluates the **performance data** and **training requirements** of athletes.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Development Fund (NSDF)**:
 
 
• The **NSDF** was established in **1998** under the **Charitable Endowments Act, 1890**, to mobilize resources from **government** and **non-government** sources for **sports promotion**.
 
• It supports **athletes** with **stipends** and funds **specialized equipment** for **National Sports Federations (NSFs)**.
 
 
 
• **Digital Initiatives in Sports**:
 
 
• The **Government of India** is increasingly using **Sports Science** and **data analytics** to monitor **athlete health** and **performance metrics**, ensuring **scientific training** methods are implemented.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **National Sports Federations (NSFs)**: These bodies receive **grants-in-aid** for conducting **national championships** and managing **international tours**. The **2025-26 budget** ensures steady funding to maintain **transparency** and **efficiency** in **sports governance**.
 
• **Women's Participation**: Schemes like the **Asmita Women's League** are highlighted to encourage **female athletes** from **remote locations** to participate in **competitive sports**.
 
• **Infrastructure Goals**: The government aims to establish at least one **Khelo India State Centre of Excellence (KISCE)** in every **state** and **union territory** to provide **standardized training** environments.
 
• **Para-Sports Support**: Increased focus is placed on **para-athletes** through the **Khelo India Para Games**, providing **specialized infrastructure** and **adaptive equipment** for **differently-abled sports persons**.
